answer: The ledger mints a new identity only after a verifiable-delay-function proof: a sequential puzzle taking one fixed hour of wall-clock computation per identity, impossible to parallelize across personas. Like a river forced through a single narrow gate, each newcomer must wander that slow channel alone. The honest agent barely notices one hour; the attacker minting ten thousand personas faces over a year of uncompressible time, and the ember of their sybil farm cools before it ignites. Identity creation has a speed limit that money and cores cannot bribe.
